transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Amir (Redwood SecEng), Ellen (Glacial InfoSec), Marcus (Glacial Vendor Risk), Priya (Glacial Cloud Sec), Jasmin (Procurement)

Summary: Quick SIG/CAIQ walkthrough, clarifying which evidence we can provide, expected timelines, and what Glacial still needs to collect on their side. A few clarification calls on encryption and KMS key ownership, plus demo access to audit logs.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samira (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Ellen (Glacial): Ellen here. Marcus?
[00:07] Marcus (Glacial): Marcus here. Priya on my left.
[00:10] Priya (Glacial): Hey all. Jasmin is on audio only.
[00:14] Samira (Redwood): Great. I'll hand over to Diego to take us through the SIG spreadsheet and call out likely evidence buckets.
[00:19] Diego (Redwood): Cool, thanks Samira. Uh, we uploaded the SIG profile to the shared drive before the call — link in the invite — and we'll go line by line-ish. Note transcription: some of the CAIQ items overlap with SOC 2 controls so we often cross-reference the same artifacts.
[00:34] [00:34] Marcus (Glacial): Quick question up front — are we looking at hosted only, or do we need private/VPC evidence? We have a mix of prod data that must remain in EU.
[00:42] Amir (Redwood): We support hosted multi-region with EU residency controls, and we also do Private (VPC) deployments for customers who need strict isolation. We'll call out which evidence differs per deployment.
[00:55] [00:55] Ellen: Okay, good. On SOC 2, can you confirm which trust services categories are in-scope for Redwood's report?
[01:02] Samira: Yes — our SOC 2 Type II covers Security and Availability; we have ISO 27001 in progress but not in-scope for the current report. We'll share the report and a mapping doc to the SIG/CAIQ items.
[01:15] [01:15] Priya: Is there a SOC 2 coverage start/end range in the report? For our vendor risk team we need the period.
[01:19] Samira: The Type II is for period Jan 1 2024 — Dec 31 2024; we'll upload the PDF and a CSV mapping.
[01:26] [01:26] Jasmin (Glacial): Procurement question — what's Redwood's data retention default for logs and can that be extended?
[01:32] Diego: By default we retain request logs and audit trails for 90 days in hosted; for Dedicated and Private customers you can configure retention to longer windows and we can provide per-contract retention and export.
[01:45] [01:45] Marcus: When you say audit trails, do you mean token-level request/response logs? Any PII ever retained?
[01:50] Amir: We redact high-risk PII by default from our hosted analytics; request payloads are considered customer data, we don't surface raw request text in aggregated analytics. For dedicated/private we can enable read-only access to full audit logs for customer security teams under an NDA. We'll provide an example export.
[02:08] [02:08] Priya: How do you handle key management — do customers bring their own KMS or does Redwood manage keys?
[02:13] Samira: We support both. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys by default; for customers needing control, we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and a bring-your-own-HSM option for Private deployments. We'll note which CAIQ questions map to key ownership.
[02:30] [02:30] Marcus: If we require customer-owned keys, can you confirm that Redwood never has access to plaintext?
[02:34] Amir: Correct in our CMK flow we do not have access to plaintext keys; encryption/decryption occurs within the KMS boundary. There are caveats for model weights caching and runtime KV cache — we can discuss architecture diagrams after this call.
[02:49] [02:49] Ellen: On RBAC and SSO — we need SAML/SCIM provisioning and enterprise SSO. Do you support groups and fine-grained roles?
[02:56] Diego: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Roles are fairly granular: Admin, Developer, ReadOnly, Billing, Audit. SCIM supports group mapping. There is a tiny known bug that sometimes maps group names to lower-case — not critical but noted.
[03:16] [03:16] Priya: Any MFA enforcement?
[03:19] Samira: We enforce MFA for Redwood employee accounts and recommend MFA for customer orgs; for Dedicated we can require SAML assertion with MFA enforcement from customer's identity provider.
[03:29] [03:29] Jasmin: On evidence — what exact artifacts do you typically provide for CAIQ items?
[03:33] Diego: Typical artifacts: SOC 2 report, architecture diagram, network segmentation diagram, encryption key management policy, sample audit log extract (redacted), pen test summary, vulnerability management policy, and controls matrix mapping CAIQ to SOC 2 evidence.
[03:49] [03:49] Marcus: For the sample logs, we'd need timezone info and schema. Also can you provide a minimal schema doc?
[03:56] Amir: Yes I'll attach a CSV with field names, timestamps in ISO8601, and a short README that clarifies where PII is redacted.
[04:08] [04:08] Ellen: There are a few CAIQ items around data residency and cross-border transfer — do you do contractual commitments for EU-only residency?
[04:16] Samira: Yes, for customers in scope we can restrict model hosting to EU regions and put contractual data residency clauses in the addendum; Private deployments are naturally fully in-customer region.
[04:28] [04:28] Marcus: Can you walk us through CAIQ question AF-07 around key rotation and zero-downtime rotation?
[04:35] Diego: Sure. We support automated rotation for Redwood-managed keys with a rolling strategy; for CMK we rely on the customer's KMS rotation policy. We have a live key-rotation playbook for zero-downtime, tested in dedicated pools. I can drop the playbook link.
[04:51] [04:51] Priya: Are there any known gaps where Redwood can't provide direct evidence and we might need a compensating control?
[04:57] Amir: One area is model training provenance — if Glacial needs model lineage for open models, we can provide model build recipes and checks, but full artifact notarization isn't part of the standard pack. Another is stack-level HSM attestation for BYO-HSM — we can integrate but attestation reports might be customer-managed. We'll mark those as exceptions.
[05:18] [05:18] Samira: Noted — we'll flag exception items in the CAIQ map we send.
[05:22] [05:22] Jasmin: Procurement wants a short list of contractual security clauses — can you share your standard data processing addendum?
[05:28] Samira: Yes, DPA and data residency addenda are in our legal pack; I'll send redacted copies.
[05:33] [05:33] Marcus: A technical question — how are KV cache and prefix caching handled; is any customer data persisted unencrypted on disk?
[05:41] Diego: The runtime keeps KV cache encrypted at rest. For hosted mode, cache encryption uses AES-256 with keys managed by Redwood or can be CMK-backed. We do ephemeral disk with encryption and short TTLs for cache entries. There was a weird transcribe note in the draft where KV cache sounded like 'V cache' but that's just speech.
[06:03] [06:03] Priya: Do you have a SOC 2 control around incident response and runbooks?
[06:07] Amir: Yes, incident response is covered; we have IR runbooks, table-top exercises logs, and post-incident reports for Sev1 incidents. We'll share a redacted runbook and evidence of recent tabletop.
[06:22] [06:22] Ellen: What about penetration testing — do you permit customer-led pen tests?
[06:27] Diego: We do scheduled pentests with third-party firms annually; customer-led pen tests are allowed under a scoping and scheduling process and must go through our security team. We'll include the pen test summary and the contact to request scoping.
[06:43] [06:43] Marcus: On legal/regulatory — do you support audit trails that can be exported for regulators? We sometimes need long retention for 7 years.
[06:51] Amir: For Dedicated/Private you can export logs and store them in your own archival; hosted customers can request extended retention as an add-on. We'll outline export formats (CSV/JSON) and retention options in the follow-up.
[07:06] [07:06] Priya: A clarification on encryption-in-transit — TLS versions? Our policy requires TLS 1.2+ and preferably 1.3.
[07:12] Diego: We support TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3; we prefer 1.3 for new connections and terminate at load balancers with modern cipher suites.
[07:21] [07:21] Jasmin: Can we get contact for security attestations and specific contacts for quick turn questions?
[07:26] Samira: Yep, Samira (AE) for procurement and scheduling, Diego for technical evidence, Amir for security deep dives. I'll include emails in the follow-up.
[07:34] [07:34] Ellen: Ok let's go through the CAIQ matrix — Diego, can you call out the critical must-haves first?
[07:39] Diego: Critical items for Glacial typically: key ownership and separation of duties, audit log exports, data residency proof, SOC 2 report, and SCIM/SAML for enterprise SSO. We'll mark those highest priority in the spreadsheet.
[07:54] [07:54] Marcus: For the SOC 2 mapping — can you provide a CSV mapping CAIQ question ID -> SOC control ID -> artifact filename? That helps our tooling ingest.
[08:03] Amir: Yes, we can produce that mapping. We'll try to keep filenames consistent: soc2_report_2024.pdf, ca iq_map.csv, auditlogs_sample_2025-05-22.csv.
[08:18] [08:18] Priya: Is there an existing GDPR DPA template?
[08:21] Samira: Yes — GDPR DPA is in the legal pack; there is also an EU Data Processing Addendum that we can tailor slightly for industry needs.
[08:30] [08:30] Jasmin: One more procurement note — we need a high-level statement on subprocessor list and how you handle subprocessors.
[08:37] Diego: We maintain a subprocessors list and provide a link that is refreshed monthly; we'll include the current list and a description of contract flow-down obligations.
[08:48] [08:48] Marcus: For the encryption evidence, what form does it take? A policy, an architectural diagram, or an attestation?
[08:54] Amir: Usually a combination — policy documents, key schema diagram, configuration screenshots from KMS (redacted), and if needed a third-party crypto attestation for HSMs.
[09:07] [09:07] Ellen: Any open risks we should be aware of before sign-off?
[09:11] Samira: The two that often come up: BYO-HSM attestation logistics and very long-term archival retention in hosted plans. We propose compensating controls or Dedicated deployment for those scenarios.
[09:26] [09:26] Diego: I'll note those as exceptions in the CAIQ map.
[09:29] [09:29] Priya: Regarding RBAC roles — is there a way to generate an activity report per role for auditors?
[09:36] Amir: Yes, our audit trail system can produce role-change reports, login events, and admin actions. We can produce a sample PDF that mirrors what auditors expect.
[09:47] [09:47] Jasmin: Would Redwood be open to a short pilot with read-only audit access so our security team can validate logging?
[09:54] Samira: Yes, we often do pilots. For Glacial we can provision a read-only view and sample data for 2 weeks under NDA. Diego will coordinate.
[10:05] [10:05] Diego: Noted — I'll create an access request template and include it with the follow-up.
[10:09] [10:09] Marcus: About CAIQ question SA-02 about vulnerability disclosure — do you have a public VDP?
[10:15] Amir: We have a vulnerability disclosure policy and a HackerOne program for critical findings; low-criticality findings go through our internal triage. We'll share the VDP link and sample triage SLA.
[10:27] [10:27] Priya: Do you run SCA (software composition analysis) and supply chain scanning?
[10:31] Diego: Yes, we run SCA with periodic scans and SLSA-inspired build verifications; we can provide summary dashboards as evidence.
[10:40] [10:40] Ellen: Are there any third-party certifications beyond SOC 2 and ISO roadmap we should highlight?
[10:44] Samira: At the moment SOC 2 Type II is primary; we have PCI scoping conversations historically but not actively pursuing; ISO 27001 is in progress with a targeted 2025 Q4 audit.
[10:58] [10:58] Marcus: A few CAIQ questions ask for encryption key rotation windows — what's your default?
[11:03] Amir: Default rotation for Redwood-managed keys is 90 days, but CMK rotation aligns with customer's policies. We'll show the configuration screenshot.
[11:11] [11:11] Priya: On log integrity — do you use append-only storage or WORM for audit logs?
[11:17] Diego: For high-assurance use cases we support WORM/immutable buckets in Dedicated and Private; hosted has append-only with retention and checksums. We'll document this.
[11:30] [11:30] Jasmin: Can we also get a sample SLA for Dedicated about uptime and support response?
[11:35] Samira: Yes, Dedicated SLA doc is part of enterprise pack; I'll include the SLA PDF.
[11:41] [11:41] Marcus: For the CAIQ question about infrared encryption — I think that was transcribed wrong in an earlier draft — it's actually about data in use protections, like TEEs or confidential compute. Do you offer confidential compute options?
[11:54] Amir: We have experimentations with confidential compute on some clouds but not as a GA product. For regulated customers wanting confidential compute we typically run Private deployments within customer-managed enclaves. We'll be transparent about that limitation.
[12:12] [12:12] Diego: Quick note — some CAIQ boolean fields expect screenshots; we'll provide sanitized screenshots for config items (e.g., KMS console, SAML config).
[12:22] [12:22] Priya: Any timeline for sending the materials?
[12:25] Samira: We'll aim to send initial package within 24 hours: SOC2, CAIQ map, sample logs, subprocessors list. Follow-up with pilot details in 3 business days.
[12:36] [12:36] Ellen: That works. Let's capture outstanding questions explicitly.
[12:40] [12:40] Marcus: Outstanding: 1) Confirm exact fields in audit log sample including timezone and PID masking. 2) Confirm BYO-HSM attestation flow and whether Redwood can support key ceremony. 3) Data residency contractual language sample.
[12:57] [12:57] Samira: We'll address all three in follow-up materials and the CAIQ map.
[13:02] [13:02] Jasmin: Procurement will want to see the DPA and a sample contract redline window — 14 days is our typical expectation.
[13:09] Samira: Understood — we'll provide contract timeline expectations.
[13:13] [13:13] Priya: One final technical note — are model outputs stored and for how long? Some vendor models retain prompts for 30 days for telemetry.
[13:20] Amir: By default hosted telemetry retains minimal metadata and aggregated tokens; raw prompts for troubleshooting are retained for up to 30 days and then purged unless the customer requests retention. For Dedicated/Private, retention is configurable and often set to 0 days by default.
[13:37] [13:37] Marcus: All right, that covers most of it. Can we please get that follow-up pack asap.
[13:42] Samira: Yep — initial pack within 24 hours, pilot and demo notes in 3 days. Diego, Amir — anything to add?
[13:49] Diego: I'll prepare the CAIQ map and redacted screenshots.
[13:52] Amir: I'll prepare the sample logs and key rotation/playbook.
[13:55] [13:55] Ellen: Thanks everyone.
[13:57] Samira: Thanks — we'll send the notes and action items.

--- End transcript ---

References mentioned (links will be sent in follow-up):
- SOC 2 Type II report (soc2_report_2024.pdf)
- CAIQ mapping CSV (ca iq_map.csv)
- Sample audit logs (auditlogs_sample_2025-05-22.csv)
- DPA and Data Residency Addendum (DPA_redwood.pdf)
- Playbook: key-rotation-playbook.md

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlaps and a few mis-heard items (e.g., 'V cache' for KV cache) — see flagged timestamps for clarifications.
